successors.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
successors.text: Kummuh with the city of Melid, which Sargon II gave to Muttallu in 712: Adiyaman Province (6,600 km2, the researcher's reading of the kingdom round Samsat) plus the city of Melid (about 250 km2)

ledger.x: 866 BC (first dated event): Kummuh appears as a kingdom.
866 BC: Qatazilu pays tribute to Ashurnasirpal II, then submits to Shalmaneser III in 858 and Kundaspi in 853.

c. 750 BC (bridged): the Assyrian tributary period ends 'in the middle of the 8th century'; the page gives no exact end, and Kustaspi is 'made to pay tribute to Sarduri II around 750 BCE'. [Fixer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: Sarduri II page opened: it does not date the end of Assyrian tribute, so the year stays a bridge.]

c. 750 BC: Kustaspi pays tribute to Sarduri II of Urartu ('around 750 BCE', page). [Fixer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: Sarduri II page: Sarduri II (reign 764-735 BC) 'expanded Urartian territory by conquering ... Melid and Kummuh in the Euphrates valley', undated.]
743 BC: Urartian hold on Kummuh broken.
738 BC: Kustaspi is a tributary of Tiglath-Pileser III ('tributary to Tiglath-pileser III in 738 and 732 BCE', page).
712 BC: Muttallu is given the city of Melid.
708 BC: Kummuh becomes an Assyrian province.
708 BC: the kingdom of Kummuh ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 708 BC').

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III against the Urartu-Arpad alliance
wars.outcome: Kustaspi of Kummuh stood in the Urartu-Arpad alliance in 743 BCE and was tributary to Tiglath-Pileser III in 738 and 732.

wars.name: Sargon II's invasion of Kummuh
wars.outcome: Sargon II accused Muttallu of allying with Urartu and invaded; the royal family and population were deported to Babylonia and Kummuh became a province.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontier or area; the shape is the modern province round Samsat.
